Findings

Wider-phone panel
Method and limits

Three independent Codex UI critics first scored the two leading references from the previous study. Three fresh critics reviewed both references and all 20 combinations at 390 pt. The same four task states showed both values, just Project, just Deadline, and a long project with an overdue timed deadline. Three more critics reviewed both references and the highest-scoring combination for each deadline treatment at 440 pt. Ties advanced the shorter populated card, then the alphabetically first layout ID. The wider panel saw a future date without a time, a task due today, empty fields and the long overdue task.

Reviewers received shuffled, anonymized screenshots. They judged whether the project communicates where the task belongs, the deadline communicates when it is due, and each can be located and edited independently. Orientation, scanability, affordance, legibility and composition each contributed zero to two points in half-point steps. Means are comparable within each panel. The wider panel changed the reviewers and fixtures as well as the width.

The prototype clock is fixed at 9:53 AM on October 16, 2026. Time remaining uses completed hours for deadlines within 48 hours and calendar days for date-only values. Today is outlined on the week strip when it falls within the displayed week. The filled day is the deadline. All designs retain the checked workspace menu, Adaptive spacing, scheduled time picker, tag area and priority cycle. The evidence covers browser prototypes at standard text size in light appearance. Native touch, keyboard behavior, VoiceOver and dark mode require separate verification.
